findings.title: Ad hoc filters are now injected multiple times because sub-requests are re-interpolated in runQuery
findings.body: runSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), which injects the request's ad hoc filters into the stream selector. However, the generated sub-requests still carry request.filters and are executed through datasource.runQuery, which interpolates the targets again with the same filters (runQuery/interpolateVariablesInQueries is unchanged by this PR). Variable replacement ($var, $__auto, step) is idempotent, but ad hoc filter injection is not: it appends matchers to the selector each time it runs, so every split sub-query is now sent to Loki with each ad hoc matcher duplicated (e.g. {a="b", env="prod", env="prod"}). In the shard-splitting path it is applied three times (runShardSplitQuery -> runSplitQuery -> runQuery); the updated shard test even bakes this in by expecting applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single query. The generated expressions are incorrect and progressively more bloated; consider stripping filters from sub-requests after the first application or making the filter injection idempotent.

findings.title: Empty-expression filter moved to before interpolation, so queries whose expr interpolates to empty are no longer dropped
findings.body: Previously runShardSplitQuery filtered query.expr AFTER interpolateVariablesInQueries ran, so a target such as { expr: '$selector' } whose variable expands to an empty string was excluded from shard splitting. The new code applies .filter((query) => query.expr) before applyTemplateVariables, so such a target now flows into groupTargetsByQueryType with an empty interpolated expr and is passed on to runSplitQuery in a sub-request. runSplitQuery filters the now-empty expr away, and if that leaves a group with no runnable targets the requests array is empty, in which case runSplitGroupedQueries throws on requests.filter(...)[0].partition (Math.max(...[]) is -Infinity, so index [0] is undefined). That exception is thrown synchronously inside the promise callback in splitQueriesByStreamShard, leaving the outer observable hanging without completing. Filter again after interpolation, or guard the empty-requests case.
